blocks.title: Key vocabulary
items: paradigm — Style or model for expressing computations.
imperative — Programming by explicit state-changing commands.
declarative — Programming by describing desired result/relations.
object-oriented — Programming using interacting objects with state and behaviour.
inheritance — A derived class reuses and specialises a base class.
override — A derived class provides its own implementation of an inherited virtual method.

blocks.title: Imperative/procedural
blocks.text: Express a sequence of state-changing instructions and reusable procedures.

blocks.title: Declarative
blocks.text: Describe a desired result or logical relationship rather than an explicit control-flow recipe.

blocks.title: Object-oriented
blocks.text: Objects group state and behaviour. Inheritance lets a derived class reuse a base class; an override replaces a virtual method. Calling that method through a base-class reference runs the actual object’s version: polymorphism .
